# 纵览原创 | 12月1日起禁售旧国标电动车！新国标电动车功能升级，价格上涨200元到500元

摄制/王思宁

**见习记者 边义婷**

12月1日起，《电动自行车安全技术规范》（GB 17761—2024）（以下简称《新国标》）将正式全面实施，市场销售车辆须全面符合《新国标》要求，未达标车辆一律不予登记上牌。

11月30日，记者探访石家庄多家电动车销售门店发现，石家庄电动自行车销售市场正处于新旧国标衔接的关键过渡期。商家对旧国标车型进行清库，并陆续上新了多款新国标车型，新国标电动车在安全性、实用性和便利性上都有所提升。

销售门店的新国标电动车。边义婷摄

“新国标电动车限速，材料的防火能力更强，孩子骑着更安全，我们家长更放心。”得知《新国标》即将实施，石家庄市民薛勇军特意来到石家庄市和平路电动车集中销售市场，想为儿子挑选一辆合适的新国标电动车。

取消脚蹬的强制性要求、塑料件不超过整车重量的5.5%、配备北斗定位系统……《新国标》对车辆的多方面作出规定。各商家根据《新国标》的各项要求，对生产工艺进行了全面升级。

在立马电动车销售门店内，4款新国标电动车已上新。银灰色的外观、合金的材质，让车型多了一些科技感。“材质上，新国标电动车使用铝镁合金代替塑料，使用寿命更长，同时还阻燃，大大降低了火灾风险。”河北立马车业科技有限公司石家庄总代理王朝说。

有顾客到门店咨询新国标电动车。边义婷摄

除此之外，新国标电动车均安装了北斗定位系统。王朝介绍，屏幕上的时间会实时更新，通过手机可查询电动车的行驶里程和位置，防盗性更好。“目前我们共研发了十几款新型国标电动车，后续还会持续更新，满足消费者的审美需求。”他说。

“这款新国标电动车多少钱？”在另一家新日电动车销售门店内，石家庄市民段祥宁询问，他担心新国标电动车在多项性能提升的同时，价格涨幅较大。

“相较于旧国标电动车，新国标电动车涨价200元到500元不等。12月1日开始，我们将把旧国标电动车全部清库，只售卖新国标电动车，还会推出优惠活动。”新日电动车销售门店店长胡兴玲说。

销售门店推出多款新国标电动车。边义婷摄

针对2025年12月1日起新国标全面实施的要求，石家庄市市场监督管理局召开全市《电动自行车安全技术规范》国家标准宣贯会，发布《关于电动自行车“新国标”实施的提醒告知书》，并联合市公安局交通管理局、石家庄市消防救援支队结合市场调研和检查时机给电动自行车销售商户发放了一份《致全市电动车经营者的一封信》。

“2025年12月1日起，市场禁止销售旧国标（GB17761—2018）电动自行车，选购请认准新国标（GB17761—2024）合规车型。”石家庄市市场监督管理局产品质量安全监督管理科二级主任科员杨彦飞为消费者提供了“选购指南”：一要看认证，务必核对车辆是否具备CCC认证标识（车身/合格证处），可扫码查询认证有效性，无认证的车型切勿购买；二要查关键性能，确认车辆电气部件、塑料件符合阻燃要求，电池组、控制器无改装痕迹；铅蓄电池车型重量≤63kg，车辆具备防篡改、智能化溯源（北斗定位/动态监测）相关设计。

“全省电动车销售门店大概有1万多家，每年销售约300万辆。”河北省自行车电动车行业协会秘书长王志认为，《新国标》实施对河北省电动自行车行业在推动行业提质升级、降低安全隐患、规范市场秩序等方面带来积极影响。

对于经营性质的物流车辆和商用车辆，王志表示，经营性车辆须安装北斗定位与动态安全监测功能，若出现车辆被盗、蓄电池温度异常或电压过高等情况，可以借助通信模块，第一时间提醒用户或消费者及时处置，提高了经营车辆使用的安全性，将进一步推动电动车消费市场规范化。

articles.title: China to ban hidden car door handles on all EVs over crash safety concerns
articles.author: Alastair McCready in Taipei
articles.clean_text:
Sleek car doors reduce vehicle drag but are prone to losing operability in the event of a crash, officials say

China will soon ban concealed door handles on electric vehicles (EVs), becoming the first country to do so after several deadly incidents triggered global scrutiny of the controversial design first popularised by [Tesla](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/tesla).

According to regulations announced on Monday by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, cars sold in China will now be required to have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of every door except the boot.

[Continue reading...](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/feb/03/china-to-ban-hidden-car-door-handles-evs)

articles.title: Electric ​cars ​go ​mainstream as ​adoption ​surges ​across ​rich and ​developing ​nations
articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.clean_text:
A wave of affordable Chinese-made EVs is accelerating the shift away from petrol cars, challenging long‑held assumptions about how transport decarbonisation unfolds

• [Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here](https://www.theguardian.com/global/2022/sep/20/sign-up-for-the-down-to-earth-newsletter-our-free-environmental-email)

Last year, almost every new car sold in Norway, the nature-loving country flush with oil wealth, was fully electric. In prosperous Denmark, which was all-in on petrol and diesel cars until just before Covid, sales of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) reached a share of 68%. In California, the share of zero-emissions vehicles hit 20%. And at least every third new car now bought by the Dutch, Finns, Belgians and Swedes burns no fuel.

These figures, which would have felt fanciful just five years ago, show the rich world leading the shift away from cars that pump out toxic gas and planet-heating pollutants. But a more startling trend is that electric car sales are also racing ahead in many developing countries. While China is known for its embrace of electric vehicles (EVs), demand has also soared in emerging markets from South America to south-east Asia. BEV sales in Turkey have [caught up](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jan/28/turkey-eu-electric-car-sales) with the EU’s, data published this week shows.

**[The Fukushima towns frozen in time: nature has thrived since the nuclear disaster but what happens if humans return?](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jan/27/japan-fukushima-environment-nuclear-disaster-nature-history-hope-loss-aoe)**

**[The UK government didn’t want you to see this report on ecosystem collapse. I’m not surprised](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jan/27/uk-government-report-ecosystem-collapse-foi-national-security)**

**[The 16-month battle to reveal the truth about Sydney Water’s poo balls](https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/jan/28/sydney-water-sewage-poo-balls-fatberg-beaches-investigation)**

**[Powering up: how Ethiopia is becoming an unlikely leader in the electric vehicle revolution](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2025/sep/12/ethiopia-electric-vehicle-power-petrol-diesel-cars-dam-green-energy)**

**[‘My Tesla has become ordinary’: Turkey catches up with EU in electric car sales](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jan/28/turkey-eu-electric-car-sales)**

**[The electric vehicle revolution is still on course – don’t let your loathing of Elon Musk stop you joining up](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jan/04/electric-vehicle-elon-musk-tesla-sales)**

[Continue reading...](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/jan/29/electric-cars-go-mainstream-as-adoption-surges-across-rich-and-developing-nations)
